surface: any /api/* path on the Kimi Code CLI local server (HTTP 429)
origin: code, HTTP status and ban window documented; the msg string is SYNTHETIC
notes: Ten authentication failures from one origin within 60 seconds trigger a 60-second ban, and this applies on NON-loopback bindings. Two consequences for a monitoring client: a retry loop against a rejected credential turns a configuration problem into a ban, so retry policy must back off and must not be implemented in the parser; and if the server is ever bound beyond loopback, plain HTTP plus a bearer token is on the network, which is a reason to keep the loopback default. Cooldown state is persisted outside the database and fail-closed on decode. The msg text is invented. Every JSON response from this server is wrapped in {code, msg, data, request_id} and the HTTP status is almost always 200, so the business result is code (0 = success) and must be checked before data. Some error envelopes carry non-empty data, which is why checking the status line or the presence of data first is wrong. request_id is an invented 26-character ULID-shaped string. The server binds plain HTTP on loopback (127.0.0.1:58627 by default) and requires a bearer token for every /api/* path except the liveness probe; that token belongs to another tool's runtime and must never be captured, stored or committed. The whole API is documented as experimental: endpoints, fields and event types may change in any version, so the /openapi.json served by the version actually in use has to be re-validated at runtime before any of these shapes is trusted.
